sentence: That same unaccented cuando shows up as the connector [Spanish uses to introduce future-oriented temporal clauses that trigger the subjunctive mood](/subjunctive-spanish/), as in Te llamaré cuando llegue (\"I'll call you when I arrive\"): a completely different function from the accented cuándo asking when something happens.
note: The current target explicitly requires subjunctive for pending future temporal clauses and contrasts cuando pueda with habitual cuando puedo; no question-mark test is asserted. Complete target body and all FAQ actually read; same-round Spanish future exact-hash read reused from lingo-b9-review/read-map.json.
target_quote: 'Spanish blocks the future and conditional forms inside temporal clauses introduced by *cuando*, *mientras*, and similar connectors, whenever the clause points at future time. RAE\'s own grammar states the restriction directly with *desde que*: only *desde que llegue* is grammatical; *desde que llegará* and *desde que llegaría* are not. The present subjunctive is what fills that gap.',
